The settings to avoid this error is by,
1. Go into the Printer Properties,
2. Go to the Settings tab on the top
3. Go to Authentication Settings...

Now when the user wants to print, they will be prompted to enter in a Department Name and Password, see below for what the prompt looks like. In my case, the department name is left blank and the user, since the user was in the Front Desk department, had the password of 105. The number was assigned and billed to the individual departments, a sheet explaining what 3 digit code was assigned to each department was posted beside this printer. After entering in password, user should be able to print.

Northstar Saflok will no longer be supported after August 2025. All key-making responsibilities will be transitioned to another managing company. Staff and guests must obtain their keys directly from that company once the transition has occurred.

  • Afterhours Tech Support (24/7 support paid by Northstar): 866-472-3565


Server Information:

Credentials:

  • Password: 1950


Northstar Saflok Specific Info:

  • Uses 3 RFID encoders:

    • 2 at the front desk

    • 1 in the housekeeping office

  • Saflok Version: Version 6


⚠️ Important: Call Saflok support before attempting any uninstall or reinstall. Each property requires a specific version, and workstations must match the server/database version. Each property has its own server, they do not share servers.


Intelity Solution Article


Troubleshooting


If NorthStar is receiving this error:


You can fix it by doing:


  1. Log into 10.0.235.245 (NorthStarSaflok server mentioned above) with your PA account
  2. Open the "Kaba Services Manager" from the Desktop
  3. Chances are one of the services is not running. Click the "Stop" button to stop all services. Then, click the "Play" button to start all services. If services will not start, then restart the Saflok server.


*This should resolve the issue. If the site is still reporting issues after this, please contact the Saflok support number listed at the top of this article.*

For the Housekeeping printers in the basement office:

The housekeeping staff needs to use the "HP Scan" app on their computers, instead of hitting the scan button on the printer. This is a workaround since scan-to-email is not working on the printers in the housekeeping office. 



For the main Konica printer in the upstairs office:

Computers need to be connected to this printer in a specific way, because they bill for printer usage separately to each department. 

Please see attached list- the printer has codes for each department to track how much they are printing. The same codes are used when copying. (Username remains blank)


When setting up a user on this printer, please add the printer as normal through the TCP/IP port. Most of the computers do not have a Konica Driver, so please install the Universal driver saved in the software share: \\ewfs1\software$\Printer Drivers\Konica Minolta

Once the driver is installed and the printer is added through TCP/IP, you need to set up the preferences to ask the user for a code each time they print: 


Settings> Click on printer> Manage> Printer properties> Settings> Authentication Settings> Enable the "Popup Authentication dialog when printing" ---> this will prompt the user for a code each time they print. They would leave the username blank.


Printer Admin settings/troubleshooting:

If the printer still isn't working after the settings above are correct, check that the SNMP is enabled:

printer properties> ports> Configure port> SNMP Status Enabled




If new codes to bill to need to be added or changed-- 

This can be done by logging into the printer's IP address:

  • Log in as admin > password: 12345678 
  • User auth/account track


Printer is set up to use Account track- keep the User Authentication OFF and the Account track ON. The codes can be viewed/edited under Account track settings. 

(If you want to enter a name more than 8 characters long, enter it into the actual printer.)

Reports for printer usage are pulled each month by Cody Sander. Both him and Tina Pacheco have the reporting program installed to their computers. 

The program is called Data Administrator-- install is in the Software share drive under the "Kelsey" folder for now. After installing, the printer needs to be configured to it. (Pending screenshots to continue article)

The reports will only save as text files, however after saving the text file, you can convert it to a CSV file for better viewing/ filtering.

https://support.office.com/en-us/article/sync-sharepoint-files-with-the-new-onedrive-sync-app-6de9ede8-5b6e-4503-80b2-6190f3354a88?ui=en-US&rs=en-US&ad=US


Sync SharePoint files with the new OneDrive sync app

SharePoint Online Office for business Office 365 Admin SharePoint Server 2019 More...

If your organization has an Office 365 business subscription or uses SharePoint Server 2019, you can sync your SharePoint files to a folder on your computer where you can work directly in File Explorer and access the files even when you're offline. Whenever you're online, any changes that you or others make will sync automatically.

Note: For information about syncing files on macOS, see Sync files with OneDrive on Mac OS X.

Set up syncing

  1. On the Office 365 app launcher, select SharePoint, and then select the site with the files you want to sync.

  2. Click Documents or navigate to the subfolder you want to sync.

  3. Click Sync. (You only need to do this once on a computer to set up syncing on that computer. After you set up syncing, the files sync automatically.)

  4. If your browser requests permission to use "Microsoft OneDrive," confirm that this is okay.

    Important: If you see a screen that says "Which library do you want to sync?", your site hasn't been set up to sync with the OneDrive sync app. If you're the IT admin for your organization, see Let users sync SharePoint files with the new OneDrive sync app. If you're not the IT admin, and your screens don't look like the ones in this article, see Sync SharePoint files with the OneDrive for Business sync app (Groove.exe) or contact your IT department.

  5. Choose the folders that you want to sync, and then click OK.

    The files will sync to a folder on your PC that has the name of your organization (for example, %userprofile%\Contoso). This folder is automatically added to the left pane in File Explorer. You can’t select to sync to a different location.

  6. To sync the files on another computer, go to that computer and follow the steps again.

Notes: 

  • You can now sync IRM-protected SharePoint and OneDrive files in your work or school account. If you’re currently syncing an IRM-protected location using the Transition from the previous OneDrive for Business sync app, stop syncing it with that sync app first. Then, install the Rights Management Service (RMS) client. When that finishes, open the SharePoint location or OneDrive in your browser and click "Sync" to begin syncing it with the sync app. 

  • If you see a lock icon on synced files in File Explorer, it means the files are synced read-only. You might not have permission to edit the files, or the library might require checkout or have required columns or metadata. If you change the files on your computer, the changes won’t sync.

  • You can't move OneNote notebooks from one site to another on your computer, and if you move other Office files between sites, version history will be lost. To move Office files, go to the site and use the Move to or Copy to command.

  • If a site name includes a character such as “:” that isn’t supported in folder names in Windows, files on the site can’t be synced.

  • If you used the previous OneDrive for Businesssync app, the folder structure for your synced folders might change when you begin syncing with the sync app. On Windows 7 computers where you used the previous OneDrive for Businesssync app, you might still see an old "SharePoint" folder under Favorites in File Explorer. You can remove the extra "SharePoint" favorite by right-clicking it and selecting Remove.

Change sync settings

To change the folders that sync for a site, or to stop syncing all files on a site, follow these steps:

  1. Select the white or blue OneDrive cloud icon in the Windows taskbar notification area.

    (You might need to click the Show hidden icons arrow next to the notification area to see the OneDrive icon. If the icon doesn't appear in the notification area, OneDrive might not be running. Click Start, type OneDrive in the search box, and then click OneDrive in the search results.)

  2. Select More > Settings.

  3. Click the Account tab to see a list of all your syncing sites.

  4. To change the folders that you're syncing, click Choose folders for that library, and then choose the folders that you want to sync. To stop syncing a site, click Stop sync next to the site. (Copies of the files remain on your computer. You can delete them if you want.)
